Subject: MAP: Skyward performance evaluation & proposed close timeline

Hi Daniel — attaching the performance benchmarking plan I promised in our MAP. The scope is focused on the generator path you'll run in production (large instruction-following prompts, expected sequence lengths ~512) and covers:

- Latency (P50/P95), TTFT (time-to-first-token), token throughput at target concurrency
- Load shape: 1/5/10/20 concurrent sessions (clients) with 8k tokens/session cap
- Quantization matrix: FP16/BF16 baseline, INT8 per-layer, INT4 aggressive profile
- Kernel profiling: per-layer kernel selection and hot-spot logs for NV GPU family
- Regression checks: token-level output diffs, hallucination probe prompts, and perplexity delta vs FP16 baseline

Deliverables: a CSV with raw measurements, kernel-profile logs, and a short summary slide included in the MAP. Proposed timeline in MAP: perf runs by Mon 3/8, internal analysis Tue 3/9, handshake + close Wed 3/10.

Please confirm the infra window on your side for the 3/6-3/8 runs and whether we can enable INT8/INT4 experimental kernels on your cluster.

Attachments: redwood-map-bench-plan.pdf

Thanks — looking forward.

— Logan Wright

Logan,

Thanks for the plan — we kicked off the lab runs yesterday. Quick status: we can give you a 48-hour window starting 03/06 22:00 UTC for the heavier concurrency runs. We're ok enabling INT8 kernels but INT4 is behind a feature flag in our runtime; would prefer to keep INT4 as a smoke/diagnostic run only.

Prelim numbers (single-node, A100-ish):
- FP16 baseline: P50 45ms, P95 120ms, TTFT 210ms, throughput 320 tokens/s at 8 concurrent
- INT8: P50 52ms, P95 140ms, TTFT 230ms, throughput 360 tokens/s at 8 concurrent
- INT4 (smoke): P50 60ms, P95 220ms, TTFT 290ms, throughput 420 tokens/s at 8 concurrent

We attached raw logs and perf CSV. Note one regression case (prompt #23) where INT4 produced a shorter completion that deviates meaningfully from FP16 — we flagged it in the CSV.

Files: perf-results-20260305.csv, kernel-profile-int8.log

I'll loop in infra to confirm availability for the 3/8 run if you need a rerun with adjusted batch sizes.

— Daniel
Principal Engineer, Skyward Inc.

Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: MAP: Skyward performance evaluation & proposed close timeline

Scoped read of the CSV and kernel logs attached. Quick technical summary:

- INT8 profile: overall latency uplift ~15% P50, 16-17% at P95 vs FP16 but throughput up ~12-15% depending on tokenization patterns. The kernel profile shows the attention backward-compatible GEMM variant selected for the majority of layers — good. No NaNs, no cache thrash.

- INT4 smoke: throughput looks good but P95 for some long prompts spikes (prompt #23, #41). Looking at kernel-profile-int8.log (INT8 run but we have INT4 smoke traces in another file), we see INT4 used a different quantized matmul kernel for the MLP layers with higher per-token variance. That matches the completion truncation seen in prompt #23 — likely quantization-induced softmax scaling differences plus a subtle tokenization boundary case.

Recommendations for MAP update:
1) Default serving profile in MAP = BF16/FP16 for first 30-day production ramp (safer quality guardrails).
2) Offer INT8 as a validated performance tier with a canary: enable INT8 on 10% of traffic for 7 days, with automated output-delta checks (we'll supply a diff harness included in MAP).
3) Keep INT4 as diagnostic only: add explicit fail-fast rules (abort on >2% token-probe regression or repeated truncation).
4) Kernel suggestion: pin the INT8 run to the "gemm-v2-stable" kernel set we used in the log — it's the lowest-variance selection we saw.

I'll draft a short technical appendix for the MAP that explains the regression heuristics and the exact metrics (KL divergence threshold, token-delta thresholds, and sample prompt list). ETA for a short appendix: EOD 3/9.

— Vivek
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtime

Subject: Re: MAP: Skyward performance evaluation & proposed close timeline

Daniel — thanks for the runs and the logs. Small update from our side after internal review:

Summary of outcomes:
- FP16/BF16 baseline numbers confirmed. INT8 shows modest latency increase but consistent throughput uplift; signal quality (per our probes) stayed within thresholds for 38/40 prompts.
- INT4 produced two regression cases (including the prompt you flagged) and larger P95 variance; recommend we treat INT4 as experimental.

Updated MAP actions and timeline (appended to MAP document; attached map-updated-20260309.pdf):
- Can you approve enabling the Canary plan (INT8 on 10% traffic) starting 2026-03-15? Canary runs for 7 days with automated diffs and rollback criteria.
- If Canary passes, full migration (INT8 preference) target: 2026-03-24.
- Procurement/contract: propose signature by 2026-03-18 to align infra scheduling and reserved capacity.

Deliverables attached: redwood-map-bench-plan.pdf (original), perf-results-20260309.csv (aggregated), kernel-profile-int8.log, map-updated-20260309.pdf (MAP appendix and rollback criteria).

Next steps: Daniel to confirm canary start window and procurement cadence; Vivek to share the appendix (EOD 3/9) and ownership for automated diff harness. I'll prepare the MAP update slide for procurement.

Thanks — excited to get this across the line.

— Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
